title: Bijectivity of the explicit tuple-generator map
statement: For a scheme $X$, a family $f_i:U_i\to U_0$ in its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], a presheaf of rings $O$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and an object $W$, put $S_\varphi=\coprod_i\{g:W\to U_i\mid g f_i=\varphi\}$. In degree $n$, the map from $\bigoplus_\varphi O(W)[S_\varphi^{n+1}]$ to the evaluated free representable Cech module sending a tuple to the coproduct injection of its free product-map generator is bijective.

source.place: Tag 03AT (lemma-cech-exact): direct-sum decomposition before the contracting homotopy; Tag 03F5 (lemma-cech-exact-modules): first proof, coefficients O(W). Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03AT and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03F5

proof.text: Evaluation preserves coproducts, and an evaluated free representable has basis the maps from W. Hence the degree n module is the free module on pairs of index tuples and maps to their product over U_0.

Associate to a product map its common composite phi and its n+1 projections. Conversely lift the tuple in Over U_0 by Pi.lift. Pi.lift_π and product uniqueness give inverse functions. Extend linearly and regroup finite support over phi. The inverse is the explicit tuple-generator map, proving bijectivity also for an empty index family or zero ring.
